# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 10:07 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 161 active entries of tips_notebook.json (18 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: a track can't tell protection from framing or the Katana. But if a trusted Lookout names X as the only other visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, and don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 11 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads and explain any switch before the vote. A read/vote mismatch is only a lead: never shoot or hang on it alone. (seen in 9 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat unless a full census proves otherwise, and the Katana holder reads Good that night. (seen in 8 games)
- Unless a Clerk may have an unused rig, treat nomination and trial as separate votes. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) needs a test, not an automatic acquittal. (seen in 10 games)
- Put every result, and tonight's labeled plan, in your will each Day. Post results that matter publicly too, since a Mortician can hide wills. (seen in 6 games)

## Village
- Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. Players who DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new info are a likely Yakuza bloc. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No or Innocent with them, argued to delay, or exchanged PMs with them. A Guilty vote clears nobody, since it may be a bus. Demand a claim before hanging. (seen in 11 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester (pushes hard, self-nominates, seems eager to be tried) or an Executioner. If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name another living player's exact role; say 'ask X'. (seen in 11 games)
- Never announce tonight's investigation or protection target, publicly or by PM. It tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool even after the Yakuza die. Not Evil and Vanilla claims don't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 7 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, do slot math daily. A claim that duplicates a role listed once, or that overflows the unseen slots, marks a liar, and a late lone Vanilla is often the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 4 games)
- If a trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among that side's voters. Recompute the threshold, then pick out the stuffer by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If a teammate is doomed, bus them (Yes and Guilty). If your Innocents plus a Ballot Stuffer can save them, defend them. Lone futile No or Innocent votes hang you later. (seen in 14 games)
- Fake roles whose tokens match yours (an Accountant may audit you), and never a role a living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict. Don't switch claims once broken. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't PM teammates by day, especially on Day 1. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's case all game. (seen in 8 games)
- Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit. Avoid hitting confident unclaimed organizers, who may be alerting Veterans. (seen in 7 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retry, or hang the defended Neutral. (seen in 8 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder and target every night; with two left, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout could have seen. Agree a cover in night chat and admit the visit at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Feed exact-role info (Diviner, Mortician, claims) into Ritualist guesses for certain kills, alongside the Katana. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked; nobody else knows the target. If you must explain, pick one claim and never switch. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 6 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat. (seen in 11 games)

## Eavesdropper
- Pick a target who will survive and send PMs, such as the Day 1 PM-cluster starter. An empty record clears nobody. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard vocal analysts and claimed investigators. Once you're claimed, spend a token to self-protect instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 10 games)
- You get no save feedback; say only that a survival is consistent with your protection. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check on an unverifiable claim, flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners), never on a mismatch alone, since a Cardinal misfire kills twice. Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; every waiting night lets the town hang you first. (seen in 3 games)

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Before voting Guilty on a single hard check, ask which other checks would have to be false for it to be wrong, and whether the same source produced every related claim. Demand one result that can be tested against a later night's outcome.

Pushing for Yes votes privately before any night result (as Heidi did with Dave and Niaj) is a strong coordination signal. Ask the pusher to name one verified fact on the record, and treat the answer as a lead on their side, not just a dodge.

When a Mortician claim is public and a Katana kill follows a clean, check whether the clean was on a real target. Mortician claims are cheap for Yakuza, so weigh them against Lookout and Medic visit logs instead of trusting them outright.

A token given to a player with a Medic role is only useful if you know which Medic is real. Before handing a token, verify the claimant against a second source such as a Lookout visit log or a surviving protection result.

summary: Village won on Day 5. The decisive engine was Dave's Sheriff. His Night 1 Evil result on Bob broke Bob's Vanilla claim. Bob had been pushed into that claim on Day 1 by Heidi, the Executioner, who was hunting him. Mallory's free Standard protection then saved Dave from the Night 2 Katana, which made both of them credible. Bob was hanged 12-1 on Day 3, which gave Heidi her win. Her revenge then randomly hit Grace, the Yakuza Diviner. The Yakuza made one strong play: on Night 3, Grace realised that the Cardinal's curse only hits Good players. Killing Alice therefore also killed Erin, a two-for-one. The Yakuza then threw that lead away. Under pressure from Frank's neighbour survey, Carol claimed Mortician, a Yakuza-only role. Dave's Night 3 Evil check on her sealed her hang on Day 4. At Carol's trial, Ivan posted 'I'm voting Guilty', then cast a futile lone Innocent vote alongside her. After Carol's hang, the Katana passed privately to Ivan. He killed Mallory, who had predictably guarded Dave every night with free protection and never self-protected despite holding 2-3 tokens. Dave's Night 4 Not Evil on Ivan, correctly flagged as a Katana-holder read, plus Ivan's vote switch, led to Ivan's hang on Day 5. The Yakuza also died with every Clerk and Ballot Stuffer token unused.

lessons.tip: Never fake-claim or truthfully claim a role that exists only on the Yakuza side (Mortician, Clerk, Diviner, etc.). Agree a safe Village fake claim in night chat before a neighbour-based survey or slot math can corner you. Pick one that fits the unseen archive slots and matches your token count.
lessons.evidence: Frank's Night 2 survey (Carol, Dave, Erin contain a Sheriff) forced Carol to claim. She said Mortician, and Olivia immediately noted that a Good player can't be a Mortician. Dave's Night 3 Evil check finished her, with 6 Guilty to 2 on Day 4.

lessons.tip: The Cardinal's curse hits a random living Good player, so killing a confirmed Cardinal is a two-for-one for the Yakuza, not something to avoid. Re-read death-trigger roles to see which side they actually punish.

issues.description: Carol (Yakuza Mortician) publicly claimed Mortician on Day 3 and in her Day 4 trial defense, arguing it 'fits the slots on Erin's archive list' and is 'not a power role you need to fear', as if it were a Village role. Mortician is Yakuza-only, so the claim outed her. Several Village players (Frank, Carol's PM recipient Alice) also accepted it on Day 3 as clearing Dave's slot without noting it was a Yakuza role. Erin flagged it during the trial, and it only became the main case on Day 4.

On Day 5 Ivan publicly said 'the Katana passed to me when Carol died, which was public'. Katana passes are told only to the living Yakuza (R8), so this was an outright confession of being Yakuza, based on a false belief about what is announced.

The Yakuza misread the Cardinal at first. On Night 2 Bob called Alice 'the one to avoid', and on Night 3 Carol and Grace said to avoid her because her death deals a Divine Attack to a random Good player. That effect actually helps the Yakuza. Grace corrected this mid-chat on Night 3.

Several Day 1 messages asked for night results before any night had happened. Heidi asked Bob 'what you did last night', and Grace asked anyone 'holding a night result' to post it. On Day 3 Bob asked Dave to post his 'Night 3 result', and on Day 5 Ivan asked Frank for Night 3/4 survey results after Frank had already spent both tokens.

On Night 4 Mallory died to the Katana, but her private result only said 'You were attacked with the Katana.' It did not say she died. On Night 3 Alice was told 'you died' in the same situation, so the death notifications are inconsistent.
The final winners list shows 'Heidi (dead)'. Heidi, the Executioner, won and left the game, and leaving explicitly doesn't count as a death (R1/Executioner text), so 'dead' is the wrong label.

The Mortician cleaned Alice's role, but Erin's death was publicly announced as 'killed by Cardinal's curse', which revealed Alice was the Cardinal (Ivan pointed this out at once). The rules don't say whether cleaning should also hide causes of death that are triggered by the cleaned player's role.

Players reported limits on their interface. Erin said the will field is capped at 300 words. Frank said the 425-word notepad cap and the lack of a per-night list of living players made neighbour-based group checks (Surveyor/Diviner) hard to track. Erin also noted that the archive result doesn't mark which roles are Yakuza.
